accessibility.alt: Three-panel infographic under the RCID v1 rule. Panel A displays the 19 estimable annual cohorts for progression failure or grade lag from 2006 to 2024: all 19 point estimates are positive, ranging from 0.94 to 28.22 percentage points, with a median of 7.18 and a Callaway and Sant'Anna student-weighted aggregate of 9.11 points whose Manski bounds span 0.43 to 16.21. Panel B shows attenuation across institutional regimes from 12.15 points in 2006–2010 and 7.82 in 2011–2015 to 5.29 in 2016–2019, 2.70 in 2020–2022, and 2.59 in 2023–2024. Panel C shows G minus 1 baseline gaps after exact matching: individual SEP eligibility is balanced at minus 1.07 points, whereas exposed students face lower school SEP agreements at minus 10.06 points, lower full-day schooling at minus 18.54 points, lower valid record coverage at minus 19.24 points, and higher prior school switching at plus 16.52 points.
accessibility.long_description: Three-panel infographic under the RCID v1 rule. Panel A displays the 19 estimable annual cohorts for progression failure or grade lag from 2006 to 2024: all 19 point estimates are positive, ranging from 0.94 to 28.22 percentage points, with a median of 7.18 and a Callaway and Sant'Anna student-weighted aggregate of 9.11 points whose Manski bounds span 0.43 to 16.21. Panel B shows attenuation across institutional regimes from 12.15 points in 2006–2010 and 7.82 in 2011–2015 to 5.29 in 2016–2019, 2.70 in 2020–2022, and 2.59 in 2023–2024. Panel C shows G minus 1 baseline gaps after exact matching: individual SEP eligibility is balanced at minus 1.07 points, whereas exposed students face lower school SEP agreements at minus 10.06 points, lower full-day schooling at minus 18.54 points, lower valid record coverage at minus 19.24 points, and higher prior school switching at plus 16.52 points. Figure 4. Historical 2006–2024 series of data-inferred closures (RCID v1), regime sub-aggregates, and G−1 NNA baseline gaps. Although the 19-cohort aggregate (+9.11 pp) and its Manski bounds (+0.43 to +16.21 pp) exclude zero, institutional and prior-mobility asymmetries at G−1 still preclude causal promotion.

decision.chart_type: Three-panel coordinated infographic: annual series, regime sub-aggregates, and NNA baseline gaps
decision.discard_condition: Discard if sign consistency across 19 cohorts is read as proof of exogenous school closure.
decision.rationale: Integrates the full 2006–2024 series with regime attenuation and G−1 institutional selection diagnostics.
rejected_alternatives: Reporting only 2016–2019: would hide sign consistency across 19 cohorts and historical attenuation.
Promoting the aggregate as a pure causal effect: would ignore JEC, SEP agreement, and prior switching gaps at G−1.

evidence.denominator: 19 estimable progression cohorts (2006–2024) and 6,190 exposed vs. 82,753 controls (2016–2019).
evidence.estimand: Exact-cell weighted ATT(g), Callaway and Sant'Anna student-weighted aggregate, and weighted baseline gap.
evidence.population: 56,862 exposed observations and 553,630 controls across 1,028 supported closure episodes (2006–2024).
evidence.question: How does progression failure vary across 2006–2024 under RCID v1, and which NNA baseline gaps persist at G−1?
evidence.transformation: Exact cell matching, student-flow depuration (RCID v1), and series-wide Manski bounds.
evidence.uncertainty: 95% school-clustered CIs, Manski bounds (+0.43 to +16.21 pp), and pre-closure institutional imbalance.
evidence.unit: Annual cohort G, institutional regime sub-aggregate, and G−1 NNA baseline gap.
